scope: Source-review and clear the four held Passport candidates (QED, Yang-Mills, GKSL/Lindblad, quantum error correction), correcting only their declared formula provenance/metadata and adding one authoritative modern-QED notation source. Existing 25 Passports and unrelated scientific/runtime records are preserved.

before.name: QED Lagrangian
before.plain: L_QED = psi-bar(i hbar c gamma D - mc^2)psi - F^2/4
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: QED Lagrangian
after.plain: L_QED = -F_mn F^mn/4 + psi-bar(i gamma^mu D_mu - m)psi
after.description: Gauge-invariant spinor QED Lagrangian in natural units before gauge fixing.
assumptions: One Dirac matter field coupled minimally to an Abelian U(1) gauge field in the displayed representative.
Natural units hbar=c=1; D_mu psi = (partial_mu + i e A_mu)psi and F_mu nu = partial_mu A_nu - partial_nu A_mu.
Gauge-fixing and ghost terms are absent from the displayed gauge-invariant classical Lagrangian; perturbative quantization requires a gauge choice.
The compact modern notation is source-locked to Tong's course notes rather than attributed verbatim to the 1949 Feynman/Dyson papers.
after.regime: Relativistic spinor quantum electrodynamics in the standard U(1) formulation. The displayed action defines the theory but does not by itself solve strong-field, bound-state or nonperturbative observables.
after.units: Natural units hbar=c=1; restore constants only after choosing a consistent unit convention for both matter and gauge terms.

sourceLocations.locator: Sec. 6.3, Eq. (6.67) / HTML Eq. (6.559), with D_mu=partial_mu+i e A_mu; Sec. 6.4 repeats the QED Lagrangian

before.name: Yang–Mills field strength
before.plain: F^a_mn = d_m A^a_n - d_n A^a_m + g f^abc A^b_m A^c_n
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Yang–Mills field strength
after.plain: F^a_mn = d_m A^a_n - d_n A^a_m + g f^abc A^b_m A^c_n
after.description: Modern Lie-algebra notation for the non-Abelian field strength; Yang and Mills wrote the original SU(2) case in isotopic-vector/matrix notation.
assumptions: Gauge potential A_mu=A_mu^a T^a takes values in a Lie algebra with [T^a,T^b]=i f^{abc}T^c under the displayed convention.
The sign of the nonlinear term follows D_mu=partial_mu+i g A_mu; changing generator or covariant-derivative conventions can flip signs or move factors of g.
Yang and Mills (1954) explicitly treat the SU(2) isotopic-spin case; the displayed f^{abc} form is its standard modern generalization.
after.regime: Classical local non-Abelian gauge field before gauge fixing/quantization. This identity alone does not establish confinement or a mass gap.
after.units: Natural-unit gauge-theory convention; dimensions depend on spacetime dimension and field normalization.

sourceLocations.locator: Phys. Rev. 96, pp. 192–193, Eqs. (4)–(9): SU(2) matrix/isotopic-vector gauge field and nonlinear field strength; modern structure-constant notation is a declared generalization

after.name: Yang–Mills Lagrangian
after.description: Pure non-Abelian gauge-field Lagrangian in standard modern normalization.
assumptions: Pure gauge sector only; matter fields and gauge-fixing/ghost terms are not included.
Generator normalization is absorbed into the component normalization giving the conventional -1/4 coefficient.
The original Yang–Mills paper uses SU(2) isotopic-vector conventions; the displayed compact component formula is a modern normalization of the same gauge-field kinetic structure.
variables: g: coupling contained in F_mu nu^a through the chosen convention
after.regime: Classical pure Yang–Mills action and starting point for quantized non-Abelian gauge theory; the Lagrangian alone is not a proof of confinement, a mass gap or QCD phenomenology.
after.units: Natural units with conventional four-dimensional field normalization.

sourceLocations.locator: Phys. Rev. 96, p. 193, Eq. (11) with the field-strength definitions developed in Eqs. (4)–(9); modern -1/4 F^a_mu nu F^{a mu nu} notation is convention-normalized

before.name: GKSL/Lindblad master equation
before.description: General Markovian completely positive trace-preserving semigroup generator.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: GKSL/Lindblad master equation
after.description: Schrödinger-picture GKSL generator for a norm-continuous completely positive trace-preserving quantum dynamical semigroup, with positive rates shown explicitly.
assumptions: Time-homogeneous quantum dynamical semigroup (Markovian semigroup) rather than general non-Markovian evolution.
Bounded/norm-continuous generator in Lindblad's theorem; finite-dimensional systems satisfy the boundedness condition automatically.
gamma_k >= 0; factors sqrt(gamma_k) can equivalently be absorbed into Lindblad operators.
Trace preservation is encoded by the anticommutator terms and complete positivity by the GKSL structure.
after.regime: Uniformly/norm-continuous CPTP semigroup dynamics. Time-dependent, memory-kernel and general non-Markovian equations are outside the theorem's semigroup scope.
after.units: H has energy units; gamma_k has inverse-time units if L_k is dimensionless; hbar is displayed explicitly in the Hamiltonian term.
after.theoryRelationship: canonical Schrödinger-picture form equivalent to the bounded-generator GKSL theorem

before.name: Knill–Laflamme error-correction condition
before.plain: P Ea† Eb P = c_ab P
before.description: Condition for a code subspace to exactly correct a set of errors.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Knill–Laflamme error-correction condition
after.plain: P Ea† Eb P = c_ab P
after.description: Basis-independent projector form of the necessary and sufficient exact quantum error-correction conditions for a specified error set.
assumptions: P projects onto the chosen code subspace and {E_a} is the specified set/span of correctable interaction/error operators.
c_ab is independent of the encoded logical state; equivalently E_a^dagger E_b acts as a scalar on the code subspace.
The condition is for exact subspace quantum error correction, not approximate correction, fault-tolerance thresholds or a claim that arbitrary errors are correctable.
variables: P: projector onto the code subspace
E_a,E_b: error/interaction operators in the correctable set
c_ab: scalar Hermitian matrix over error labels
after.regime: Exact subspace quantum error correction for a declared error set/channel operator span. Approximate/operator-algebra QEC use generalized conditions.
after.theoryRelationship: necessary and sufficient exact recovery condition in compact projector form

sourceLocations.locator: arXiv:quant-ph/9604034v1, Sec. 2 Eqs. (6)–(7), PDF pp. 5–6; Sec. 3 formalizes the necessary/sufficient recovery conditions. P E_a†E_b P=c_ab P is the basis-independent rewrite.

before.name: Stabilizer-state condition
before.description: A stabilizer state or code lies in the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of its stabilizer generators.
before.regime: Canonical representative within the linked theory or framework; consult the linked source for detailed domain assumptions.
before.units: Unit convention follows the linked source; constants are shown explicitly where present.

after.name: Stabilizer-state condition
after.description: A stabilizer state or code lies in the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of its stabilizer generators.
assumptions: S is an Abelian subgroup of the n-qubit Pauli group that does not contain -I for a nonempty code space.
Code states are simultaneous +1 eigenstates of every stabilizer element; it is sufficient to impose the condition on an independent generating set.
This characterizes stabilizer codes, an important subclass of quantum error-correcting codes, not all QEC codes.
variables: |psi>: code state fixed by all stabilizer generators
after.regime: Qubit stabilizer-code formalism. Nonadditive, bosonic and other non-stabilizer codes require different structures.
after.theoryRelationship: defining common +1 eigenspace condition for stabilizer codes

sourceLocations.locator: Gottesman thesis (1997), Ch. 3 Sec. 3.2, general stabilizer code: codewords are the simultaneous +1 eigenspace of the Abelian stabilizer group

addedPassportRecords.scientificStatus: established theory with extremely precise perturbative tests in its applicable regimes
addedPassportRecords.coreIdea: Charged Dirac matter couples locally to an Abelian U(1) gauge field; the gauge principle fixes the interaction structure while quantization yields photons, charged fermions and their scattering/loop corrections.
addedPassportRecords.degreesOfFreedom: A U(1) gauge potential A_mu (photon field) and charged Dirac spinor fields, with gauge redundancy removed by a quantization/gauge-fixing prescription when computing observables.
assumptions: The displayed defining Lagrangian uses one spin-1/2 charged matter field in natural units; realistic QED may include several charged species.
Local U(1) gauge invariance and minimal coupling define the classical interaction structure; perturbative calculations additionally require gauge fixing and renormalization.
The compact modern Lagrangian is source-locked to Tong's Cambridge notes; Feynman and Dyson remain historical primary sources rather than verbatim provenance for that notation.
Perturbative success at small electromagnetic coupling is not a proof of convergent perturbation theory or exact solvability at arbitrary fields/energies.
addedPassportRecords.mathematicalStructure: Abelian gauge theory with F_mu nu=partial_mu A_nu-partial_nu A_mu, D_mu=partial_mu+i e A_mu, a Dirac action and gauge-field kinetic term; perturbative observables use gauge-fixed propagators, vertices and renormalized correlation functions.
addedPassportRecords.regime: Relativistic electromagnetic interactions where QED is the appropriate low-energy gauge theory. Electroweak unification, hadronic structure and genuinely nonperturbative strong-field settings require additional physics or methods.
predictionsConsequences: Photons mediate electromagnetic interactions between charged quantum fields and appear as gauge-field quanta with two physical polarizations.
Perturbative amplitudes include virtual-particle and loop corrections organized by the electromagnetic coupling.
Gauge invariance enforces Ward-type identities and constrains allowed interactions.
addedPassportRecords.evidenceSummary: This Passport source-reviews the formal QED structure and does not add a new experimental Evidence record. Precision QED experiments are a separate empirical layer and should be represented by source-specific Evidence records before being summarized as app evidence.
addedPassportRecords.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: The defining Lagrangian and perturbative formalism do not by themselves establish convergence at all orders, exact nonperturbative solvability, or the validity of QED beyond the domain where electroweak/hadronic effects become relevant.
limitations: Gauge fixing and renormalization are required for practical perturbative calculations but are not shown in the compact defining Lagrangian.
QED is embedded in the electroweak Standard Model at higher energies and is not a theory of strong or weak interactions.
Bound states, very strong external fields and infrared/collinear observables can require resummation or specialized nonperturbative techniques.
usefulDiscriminators: Abelian versus non-Abelian self-interaction: the photon field strength lacks the gauge-boson self-coupling term present in Yang–Mills theory.
Gauge group, matter representation and coupling structure when comparing QED with electroweak and QCD sectors.
Observable precision tests must be matched to the perturbative/resummation order and hadronic/electroweak corrections used.
unresolvedQuestions: How should strongly coupled or nonperturbative QED regimes be computed with controlled uncertainties in the relevant physical setting?
How do infrared structure and resummation choices affect precision observables beyond fixed-order perturbation theory?

Sec. 5.5 Eq. (5.35): Dirac Feynman propagator; Sec. 6.5 repeats it as the QED internal fermion line
Historical primary source for the space-time/Feynman formulation of QED; not used as verbatim provenance for the modern compact Lagrangian notation
Historical primary source establishing equivalence and perturbative organization of the Tomonaga–Schwinger/Feynman formulations; not a verbatim modern-Lagrangian citation

addedPassportRecords.sourceVersion: Modern equations follow David Tong's Cambridge QFT notes in natural units; 1949 Feynman/Dyson papers are retained for historical/program provenance.

addedPassportRecords.scientificStatus: established foundational gauge-theory framework; pure-theory nonperturbative questions remain
addedPassportRecords.coreIdea: Local non-Abelian gauge symmetry introduces Lie-algebra-valued gauge fields whose field strength contains gauge-boson self-interactions, providing the structural basis for modern non-Abelian gauge theories.
addedPassportRecords.degreesOfFreedom: Gauge potentials A_mu^a valued in a Lie algebra, with redundant gauge coordinates; matter fields may be added in chosen group representations but are absent from the pure-gauge Lagrangian card.
assumptions: A specified Lie group/algebra and generator normalization define the modern component notation.
Yang and Mills (1954) formulate the original SU(2) isotopic-spin case; the atlas structure-constant equations are an explicitly declared generalization.
The displayed pure-gauge Lagrangian omits matter, gauge-fixing and ghost terms.
A classical gauge Lagrangian does not by itself prove confinement, a quantum mass gap or the phenomenology of QCD.
addedPassportRecords.mathematicalStructure: Non-Abelian connection A_mu, covariant derivative and curvature F_mu nu=dA+g A∧A; the pure action is quadratic in F while F itself is nonlinear in A, generating gauge-boson self-couplings after quantization.
addedPassportRecords.regime: Local non-Abelian gauge theories and the pure-gauge sector underlying QCD/electroweak constructions; detailed quantum predictions require gauge fixing, renormalization and often nonperturbative methods.
predictionsConsequences: Gauge bosons carry the non-Abelian charge and self-interact through the nonlinear field strength.
Matter representations couple through the same gauge connection once a representation is specified.
The same formal gauge principle extends beyond the original SU(2) isotopic example to general compact gauge groups used in particle physics.
addedPassportRecords.evidenceSummary: This Passport source-reviews the theoretical construction. It does not add an experimental Evidence record and does not treat QCD confinement or the Yang–Mills mass gap as experimentally/theoretically established by the 1954 paper alone.
addedPassportRecords.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: The original gauge principle and classical equations do not prove confinement, asymptotic freedom, a mass gap, or that a particular non-Abelian gauge group describes nature without additional matter content and empirical evidence.
limitations: Pure Yang–Mills omits fermion/scalar matter and spontaneous symmetry breaking used in realistic Standard-Model sectors.
Gauge fixing and ghosts enter perturbative quantization although they are absent from the gauge-invariant classical action.
Nonperturbative infrared dynamics cannot be inferred solely from the classical field equations.
usefulDiscriminators: Presence of non-Abelian structure constants and gauge-boson self-interactions versus Abelian QED.
Choice of gauge group and matter representations when distinguishing QCD/electroweak realizations.
Perturbative running and nonperturbative observables require quantum calculations beyond the defining action.
unresolvedQuestions: How can nonperturbative pure Yang–Mills observables be computed with rigorous continuum control?
How should continuum and lattice descriptions be connected quantitatively across strongly coupled regimes?

sourceLocations.locator: Phys. Rev. 96 (1954), pp. 192–193: isotopic gauge transformation and covariant derivative; Eqs. (4)–(9) define the SU(2) nonlinear field strength; Eq. (11) gives the gauge-invariant Lagrangian density

addedPassportRecords.sourceVersion: Yang & Mills (1954) original SU(2) isotopic-gauge conventions; atlas formulas state the standard modern Lie-algebra component generalization explicitly.

addedPassportRecords.scientificStatus: established structural theorem for norm-continuous Markovian quantum dynamical semigroups
addedPassportRecords.coreIdea: Time-homogeneous completely positive trace-preserving semigroup dynamics have a generator consisting of a Hamiltonian commutator plus a constrained dissipative term, giving the canonical GKSL/Lindblad master-equation structure.
addedPassportRecords.degreesOfFreedom: A reduced-system density operator, a Hermitian effective Hamiltonian and system operators that encode dissipative channels/rates; the environment has already been eliminated into the generator.
assumptions: The reduced dynamics form a time-homogeneous quantum dynamical semigroup with complete positivity and trace preservation.
Lindblad's theorem assumes a bounded/norm-continuous generator on B(H); finite-dimensional systems fall inside this setting.
Positive rates may be absorbed into rescaled Lindblad operators, so many algebraically equivalent operator bases represent the same generator.
General non-Markovian, memory-kernel or explicitly time-dependent evolution is not characterized by this semigroup theorem.
addedPassportRecords.mathematicalStructure: Generator of a CPTP semigroup: Hamiltonian derivation plus completely dissipative quadratic operator terms. Lindblad Theorem 2 gives the Heisenberg generator and its dual Schrödinger-picture master equation.
addedPassportRecords.regime: Markovian semigroup open-system dynamics, especially finite-dimensional or bounded-generator settings; microscopic derivations may impose additional weak-coupling/coarse-graining approximations.
predictionsConsequences: If a model satisfies the theorem's assumptions, its reduced dynamics preserve positivity even when the system is entangled with an arbitrary ancilla.
Dissipative channels generate relaxation, dephasing and other irreversible reduced-system behavior while maintaining trace preservation.
Different operator representations can describe the same physical generator after basis transformations and rate rescaling.
addedPassportRecords.evidenceSummary: The attached sources establish the mathematical generator structure, not an experimental observation. Whether a concrete physical system is accurately Markovian/GKSL is an additional modeling and empirical question.
addedPassportRecords.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: The GKSL theorem does not say every open quantum system is Markovian, that a fitted Lindblad model uniquely identifies its microscopic bath, or that arbitrary non-Markovian dynamics can be rewritten as one time-independent semigroup generator.
limitations: Memory effects, strong system–bath correlations and time-dependent environments can violate the semigroup assumptions.
Unbounded generators/operators require domain analysis beyond the bounded theorem quoted here.
A phenomenological Lindblad fit can reproduce data without uniquely revealing the microscopic reservoir.
usefulDiscriminators: Check CP divisibility/time-homogeneous semigroup assumptions before applying the theorem as a physical model.
Compare inferred decay/dephasing rates against microscopic bath calculations and non-Markovian alternatives.
Test whether one time-independent generator reproduces multi-time/initial-state behavior, not only a single decay curve.
unresolvedQuestions: Which microscopic regimes justify a controlled GKSL reduction for a given experimental platform?
How should model selection distinguish genuine memory effects from time-dependent Markovian rates or parameter drift?

sourceLocations.locator: Commun. Math. Phys. 48 (1976), Theorem 2, Eqs. (4.2)–(4.3), p. 128: bounded generator on B(H) and dual state-space form
J. Math. Phys. 17 (1976), pp. 821–825: establishes the general generator form for completely positive dynamical semigroups of finite N-level systems

addedPassportRecords.sourceVersion: Lindblad (1976) theorem statement and GKS (1976) finite-N result; displayed atlas equation is the equivalent Schrödinger form with nonnegative rates shown explicitly.

addedPassportRecords.scientificStatus: established framework for protecting specified logical information against specified error sets
addedPassportRecords.coreIdea: Encode logical states into a larger physical Hilbert space so that correctable errors leave no distinguishable imprint of the logical state in the error syndrome, permitting recovery without measuring the unknown logical amplitudes.
addedPassportRecords.degreesOfFreedom: A logical/code subspace with projector P, physical Hilbert-space degrees of freedom, a specified set/span of error operators and a recovery channel; stabilizer codes add commuting Pauli-group constraints as a structured subclass.
assumptions: Correctability is always relative to a declared code subspace and error/operator span; no finite code corrects arbitrary unrestricted errors.
The Knill–Laflamme condition here concerns exact subspace recovery; approximate error correction uses relaxed criteria.
Stabilizer codes are an important subclass of QEC, not the general form of every quantum code.
Fault-tolerant computation additionally constrains how gates, syndrome extraction and correlated faults propagate; it does not follow from the bare correction condition alone.
addedPassportRecords.mathematicalStructure: Exact correction is characterized by P E_a† E_b P=c_ab P (basis-independent form of Knill–Laflamme's logical-state conditions). Stabilizer codes describe code spaces as simultaneous +1 eigenspaces of commuting Pauli-group generators.
addedPassportRecords.regime: Finite-dimensional subspace quantum error correction for specified noise/error spans; operator-algebra, bosonic/continuous-variable and approximate codes generalize the framework.
predictionsConsequences: Errors satisfying the Knill–Laflamme condition can be reversed on the code without learning the encoded amplitudes.
Error syndromes can distinguish correctable error sectors while preserving logical coherence.
Structured stabilizer codes allow efficient algebraic descriptions of many useful QEC constructions.
addedPassportRecords.evidenceSummary: This Passport source-reviews the mathematical correction criteria. It does not add a new experimental Evidence record or claim a fault-tolerance threshold for any hardware platform.
addedPassportRecords.whatEvidenceDoesNotEstablish: The existence of an exact code condition does not establish that a given device reaches fault-tolerant logical error rates, that all physical noise lies in the modeled correctable set, or that stabilizer codes exhaust quantum coding possibilities.
limitations: Performance depends on the actual noise channel, encoding overhead, syndrome measurement fidelity and decoder/recovery implementation.
Approximate/coherent/correlated errors can require metrics beyond exact correctability.
Fault tolerance and scalable logical computation require circuit-level architecture and threshold analyses beyond static code conditions.
usefulDiscriminators: Evaluate logical error channels under the measured physical-noise model rather than code distance alone.
Distinguish exact algebraic correctability from approximate logical fidelity and from fault-tolerant threshold claims.
Compare code families at fixed physical resources, decoder assumptions and correlated-noise model.
unresolvedQuestions: Which code/decoder architectures provide the best logical performance for realistic biased, correlated and leakage-dominated noise?
How should exact Knill–Laflamme structure be generalized and benchmarked for approximate or subsystem/operator-algebra codes in hardware?
